string.text: Loudness of the teleport sound when a hunter breaks off or vanishes. 0 mutes it. Default 40.

Monolith whispers in your head while a named hunter is within 60 m, louder the closer he is. A named hunter is the main Nemesis enemy: hard to kill, he retreats when hurt and comes back stronger. 0 mutes the whispers. Default 60.
Loudness of the radio static that comes with the arrival warning. 0 mutes it (the PDA line still shows). Default 70.
A radio message and static warn you 30 to 120 seconds before a hunt starts. Off: the hunt starts without warning. Default on.
Name of the boss, a rare and stronger named hunter. Other hunters always get random names. Default: Bogdan Kravets

Chance that a named hunter is the boss: a tougher, cloaked hunter with his own look and messages. Only one boss at a time, at most one a day. Beating a hunt he was in makes the next hunt 2 cycles weaker. Default 2.
How much tougher the boss is than a normal named hunter. 0 = no tougher. Default 30.
In-game days after the grace period before a boss can appear. Default 3.

Chance that a boss, when he spawns, tries to sneak up behind you instead of charging. If he gets within 20 m behind you unseen, he tells you so, and attacks 5 seconds later. A hit breaks the sneak. Default 50.
Use the high definition portrait on PDA messages. Off uses the original low definition icon.
For testing: hunts start sooner (no grace period, 180 seconds between hunts) and can spawn anywhere, even near traders and bases. Turn it off for normal play.
Tick and apply: one Nemesis PDA message is sent at once, with the banner icon and the PDA sound. With Debug logs on, the console says whether it went out. The box unticks itself.
Force a boss in the next hunt
For testing. Tick and apply: the next named hunter to spawn is the boss, ignoring the chance, the day limit and the once-a-day rule. The box unticks itself.
Write Nemesis diagnostic and error lines to the console. Leave this off unless you are tracking a problem. Lines that start with an exclamation mark are errors.
In-game days before the first hunt of a new game (or after installing the mod). Default 12.
In-game hours after a hunt ends before the next one can start. 0 = as soon as possible. Default 24.
If you survive this many in-game hours, the hunters give up and teleport away, and the next hunt is not stronger. Default 4.
A named hunter breaks off and teleports away when his health drops this low. It gets lower each cycle, so he fights longer every time. Default 25.

Each hunt you beat makes the next one stronger. That step is called a cycle. This sets how much stronger each cycle is: higher means he takes less damage and retreats later. 1.0 = no growth. Default 1.1.
The most the hunters can ever scale up, however many hunts you beat. Higher = tougher late hunts. Default 3.
Reset escalation when a hunter kills you
If a hunter kills you, the hunts go back to their starting strength (cycle 1), even when you reload a save. Default on.
Tick and apply to set the hunts back to their starting strength (cycle 1) right now. The box unticks itself.
Every this many in-game days after the last hunt ended, the hunters get one cycle weaker (never below cycle 1). 0 = never. Default 1.
How fast named hunters' armour catches up with yours. 0 = normal (full after about 10 hunts). Higher = faster, lower = slower. Regular squad members are not affected. Default 0.
How much higher than yours a named hunter's ballistic rating (BR) can get. Default 0.20. 1.0 = almost bulletproof.
How much more damage, in percent, a named hunter's armour can block than yours. Default 25. He never blocks more than 90 percent.
Turn on only if you use the Obrien GAMMA Overhaul mod. It makes hunters read your armour the way that mod does. Default off.
On: when a hunter loses track of you, he searches where he last saw or heard you, and finds you again after 60 seconds. Off: he always knows where you are. Default on.

Extra squad members approach from the sides on clear lanes instead of running straight at you, and those carrying sniper rifles stop short and take a firing position. Named hunters still come straight for you. Default on.
Before teleporting away, a hurt hunter first runs to nearby cover for up to 4 seconds. He cannot be hurt while he runs. Default on.

Named hunters turn invisible while they stalk you from more than 30 m, and reappear when they fight, get within 15 m or are hit. At most once every 20 seconds. Uses the same invisible model as the teleport. Experimental: a held weapon may stay visible. Default on.
Hunters stop chasing and start fighting when they see you, or any other enemy, this close. Default 70.
Hunters never spawn closer to you than this. Default 70.
The farthest from you a hunt can spawn. Default 140.
Relative chance the hunt is only the hunter. These five sliders are weights, not percents, so they do not need to add up to 100. Default 50.
Relative chance he brings one extra normal stalker. The extra can be killed. Default 25.
Relative chance of two extras with him. Default 14.
Relative chance of three extras with him. Default 10.
Relative chance of four extras with him. Default 6. Set a weight to 0 to stop that squad size.

Chance that each extra squad member is another named hunter instead of a normal stalker. Named hunters carry a rank in their name, are hard to kill, retreat when hurt and never leave a body. 0 = only the leader is named, 100 = the whole squad. Default 25.
